messages:
alex: Quick lunchtime brain game — pick a song that feels like the opening line of a book you love. Ill start: 'Call me Ishmael.' Song: 'Ocean Breathes Salty' — Modest Mouse :ocean:
maria: Book: 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.' Song: 'Bittersweet Symphony' — perfect slow-motion city energy :violin:
chris: Book: 'All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.' Song: 'How to Disappear Completely' — Radiohead. Quietly unsettled.
jamie: Book: 'In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.' Song: 'Also sprach Zarathustra' (2001 theme). Overly dramatic but iconic :laughing:
sophie: Book: 'The first thing I remember is the smell of my father’s hands.' Song: 'Father and Son' — tender, a little painful.
noah: Book: 'It was a pleasure to burn.' Song: 'Burn' — Ellie Goulding. Cheesy but literal :fire:
chris: @noah haha that one slaps, imagining firefighters dancing.
maria: Curveball: Book: 'The man in black fled across the desert, and the gunslinger followed.' Song: 'Wayfaring Stranger' — dusty, wandering folk.
alex: We should make a 10-track "first-lines" playlist. Who wants to build it? :headphones:
jamie: Ill assemble tonight. DM me Spotify links before 8pm. No judgment on guilty pleasures :grimacing:
sophie: This would be a fun offsite icebreaker — round-robin: line + 30s of the song.
lunch-bot: It’s 12:36 — sandwich reminder :sandwich: (automated)
noah: Sent my link to @jamie. Anyone else?
